report_slots = FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter(2, name="reports", wait=2, retry_after=3)


@api.get("/orders", dependencies=[Depends(api_budget())])
async def orders(user: User) -> list[Order]:
    return [Order(id=n, customer=user, total=12.5 * n) for n in range(1, 4)]


async def render_report(user: str, month: str) -> Report:
    """Stands in for the slow part: rendering a PDF, OCR, a call to an AI model."""
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    return Report(customer=user, month=month, pages=12)


# The budget before the slots: a client over its budget is refused at once, instead of waiting
# for a slot first.
@api.post("/reports", dependencies=[Depends(api_budget(cost=10)), Depends(report_slots)])
async def create_report(report: ReportRequest, user: User) -> Report:
    """10 of the user's 30 a minute, and one of the 2 slots while it renders."""
    return await render_report(user, report.month)


app.include_router(api)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Errors and observability
docs.text:
Errors and observability Client to Your app: POST /orders, invalid. Your app to Client: 422, problem details. Client to Your app: GET /orders/3/invoice. Your app to Logs: traceback, request_id. Your app to Client: 500, nothing about it. Client to Your app: GET /reports/sales. Your app to Client: 504 at the deadline. Clear errors, nothing leaked, one ID in every log line. Client Your app Logs POST /orders, invalid 422, problem details GET /orders/3/invoice traceback, request_id 500, nothing about it GET /reports/sales 504 at the deadline Clear errors, nothing leaked, one ID in every log line What it's for: errors that clients can act on without learning anything about the server, a request ID that ties a complaint to its log lines, and a deadline for every request.

An orders API that is easy to operate. Its errors are RFC 9457 problem details, from FastAPIProblemDetails: a validation error says where and what without echoing what was sent, running out of stock is a Problem with an available member, and a bug is a bare 500 that tells the client nothing about it. RequestIDMiddleware gives every request an ID, which RequestIDLogFilter puts in every log line, uvicorn's included, and which comes back in a header and in every problem.

RequestTimeoutMiddleware gives every request a deadline: the slow sales report gets a 504 and its database connection back, while the CSV export streams for as long as it takes. health_router adds the probes of the load balancer, with the database as a critical check and the cache as a non-critical one. OpenTelemetry needs no code: under its zero-code instrumentation, Alcazaba's metrics and spans go out with the app's (Metrics and traces).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
python examples/observability/main.py

That starts uvicorn with the example's LOGGING configuration, so that every log line carries the request's ID. uvicorn examples.observability.main:app serves the same app with uvicorn's default logging, without the IDs; to use the configuration with the uvicorn command, save it as JSON and pass --log-config.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
An order placed. The response has an X-Request-ID, and so does every line logged for it:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 1, "quantity": 2}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef

{"product_id":1,"quantity":2,"id":31}

2026-10-26 12:34:23,679 INFO [efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef] orders: Order 31 placed
2026-10-26 12:34:23,680 INFO [efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef] "POST /orders HTTP/1.1" 201 Created

A validation error says which field is wrong and why, but not what was sent: FastAPI's own answer would echo the input, passwords included.

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 1, "quantity": "lots"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content
x-request-id: f25fd411982ef2db845915fd6c6591b6
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Unprocessable Content","status":422,"instance":"/orders","errors":[{"loc":["body","quantity"],"msg":"Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer","type":"int_parsing"}],"request_id":"f25fd411982ef2db845915fd6c6591b6"}

Running out of stock is a problem of the API's own, with its type and an available member that a client can act on:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 2, "quantity": 5}'
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
x-request-id: 3905c40b8fa0c37707adf6b910773f47
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"https://example.com/problems/out-of-stock","title":"Out of stock","status":409,"detail":"Only 3 left","instance":"/orders","available":3,"request_id":"3905c40b8fa0c37707adf6b910773f47"}

A bug: the invoice's PDF renderer refuses the connection, and nothing handles it. The client gets a bare 500 with nothing about the renderer, and the request ID to quote. Here the client sent the ID itself, as a proxy would, and it was kept:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/3/invoice -H "X-Request-ID: support-ticket-4512"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
x-request-id: support-ticket-4512
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Internal Server Error","status":500,"instance":"/orders/3/invoice","request_id":"support-ticket-4512"}

The server logs the traceback under that ID:

2026-10-26 12:34:23,692 INFO [support-ticket-4512] "GET /orders/3/invoice HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
2026-10-26 12:34:23,692 ERROR [support-ticket-4512] uvicorn.error: Exception in ASGI application
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../examples/observability/main.py", line 140, in invoice
    raise ConnectionError(f"pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order {order_id}")
ConnectionError: pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order 3

The sales report takes 30 s. At the 10 s deadline the query is cancelled, its connection goes back to the pool and the client gets a 504. The middleware answers it itself, and with FastAPIProblemDetails installed its answer is a problem too:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/sales
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-id: 7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Gateway Timeout","status":504,"detail":"Request timed out","instance":"/reports/sales","request_id":"7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e"}

2026-10-26 15:22:34,756 WARNING [7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e] fastapi_alcazaba.observability.timeouts: GET /reports/sales timed out after 10.0s: answered 504

The export has no deadline: its 30 rows stream for 15 s, and it isn't cut short.

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download} bytes in %{time_total}s\n' \
    http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/export
200 text/csv; charset=utf-8 231 bytes in 15.539356s

The probes. Readiness runs the checks and says how each went; liveness only says that the process answers:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: no-store
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: 577fa3fd67c00a6bd4b80cbf29256384

{"status":"ok","checks":{"database":{"status":"ok","duration_ms":0.014},"cache":{"status":"ok","duration_ms":0.012}}}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/live
{"status":"ok"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The order of the middlewares: the last one added is the outermost. RequestIDMiddleware goes around the deadline, so that the 504 has an ID too. A 500 is answered outside every middleware, by Starlette, and FastAPIProblemDetails adds the ID to it itself.
  • The filter on the handlers: a logger's filters don't see the records of its children, so RequestIDLogFilter goes on both handlers of the logging configuration, and uvicorn's access and error lines get the ID along with the app's.
  • Nothing to learn from an error: validation errors never carry the input, the 500 says nothing about the renderer, and the database's db.internal:5432: connection refused would be logged by the readiness check, never returned to a public probe.
  • A deadline gives resources back: the connection is a yield dependency, so it goes back to the pool when the deadline cancels the request. The export is exempt (paths={"/orders/export": None}): once a response has started it can't become a 504, it would only be cut short.
  • Critical or not: a failing database makes /health/ready a 503 and takes the process out of the load balancer; a failing cache only makes it degraded, since the cache fails open and taking every process out would turn its outage into a full one.
  • OpenTelemetry without code: run the app under opentelemetry-instrument. The FastAPI instrumentation traces each request, and Alcazaba's metrics (fastapi_alcazaba.problems, .request_timeouts, .request_ids, .health.checks…) go out through the same SDK.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/observability/main.py
"""An orders API that is easy to operate: errors, request IDs, deadlines and health checks.

    python examples/observability/main.py  # uvicorn, with the logging configuration below

- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`): a validation error says where
  and what, never the values sent; running out of stock is a `Problem` with an `available`
  member; a bug is a bare 500 that tells the client nothing about it.
- Every request has an ID, in the `X-Request-ID` response header, in every problem and in every
  log line, uvicorn's included: a client quotes it, and its lines are found in the logs.
- Every request has a deadline: the slow sales report gets a 504 and its database connection
  back, while the CSV export streams for as long as it takes.
- `/health/live` and `/health/ready` for the load balancer: the database is a critical check, the
  cache a non-critical one.

OpenTelemetry needs nothing here. Run the app under its zero-code instrumentation
(`opentelemetry-instrument`, see "Metrics and traces" in the guide): the FastAPI instrumentation
traces each request, and Alcazaba's metrics (problems, request_timeouts, request_ids,
health.checks...) go out through the meter of the app's cache.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache, FastAPIProblemDetails, Problem
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.observability import (
    RequestIDMiddleware,
    RequestTimeoutMiddleware,
    health_router,
)

logger = logging.getLogger("orders")

LOG_FORMAT = "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(request_id)s] %(name)s: %(message)s"
ACCESS_FORMAT = '%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(request_id)s] "%(request_line)s" %(status_code)s'
# uvicorn's log_config. The filter goes on every handler (a logger's filters don't see the records
# of its children), so uvicorn's access and error lines carry the ID too. Plain JSON: for the
# uvicorn command, save it to a file and pass --log-config.
LOGGING: dict[str, Any] = {
    "version": 1,
    "disable_existing_loggers": False,
    "filters": {
        "request_id": {"()": "fastapi_alcazaba.observability.RequestIDLogFilter"},
    },
    "formatters": {
        "default": {"format": LOG_FORMAT},
        "access": {"()": "uvicorn.logging.AccessFormatter", "fmt": ACCESS_FORMAT},
    },
    "handlers": {
        name: {
            "class": "logging.StreamHandler",
            "formatter": name,
            "filters": ["request_id"],
        }
        for name in ("default", "access")
    },
    "loggers": {
        "uvicorn.access": {"handlers": ["access"], "level": "INFO", "propagate": False},
    },
    "root": {"handlers": ["default"], "level": "INFO"},
}


class NewOrder(BaseModel):
    product_id: int = Field(gt=0)
    quantity: int = Field(gt=0, le=100)


class Order(NewOrder):
    id: int


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database and its connection pool."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.stock = {1: 25, 2: 3}  # units left, by product
        self.orders = [Order(id=n, product_id=1, quantity=1) for n in range(1, 31)]
        self.in_use = 0  # connections taken from the pool
        self.up = True
        self.report_seconds = 30.0  # the sales report is a slow query
        self.row_seconds = 0.5  # and the export reads its rows slowly

    async def ping(self) -> None:
        if not self.up:
            # What drivers say: a host and a port that a public probe mustn't show anyone.
            raise ConnectionRefusedError("db.internal:5432: connection refused")


async def connection(request: Request) -> AsyncIterator[Database]:
    """A connection from the pool, given back when the request ends, also when it times out."""
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    db.in_use += 1
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.in_use -= 1


DB = Annotated[Database, Depends(connection)]
router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def place_order(new: NewOrder, db: DB) -> Order:
    if new.product_id not in db.stock:
        raise HTTPException(
            status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            "No such product",
        )  # a 4xx's detail is sent
    available = db.stock[new.product_id]
    if new.quantity > available:
        raise Problem(
            status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            f"Only {available} left",
            type="https://example.com/problems/out-of-stock",
            title="Out of stock",
            extensions={"available": available},
        )
    db.stock[new.product_id] -= new.quantity
    order = Order(id=len(db.orders) + 1, **new.model_dump())
    db.orders.append(order)
    logger.info("Order %d placed", order.id)  # the filter adds the request's ID
    return order


@router.get("/orders/export")
async def export_orders(db: DB) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Every order as CSV, sent as the rows are read. It has no deadline (see `paths` below): once
    a response has started it can't become a 504, it would only be cut short."""

    async def rows() -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        yield "id,product_id,quantity\n"
        for order in list(db.orders):
            await asyncio.sleep(db.row_seconds)
            yield f"{order.id},{order.product_id},{order.quantity}\n"

    return StreamingResponse(rows(), media_type="text/csv")


@router.get("/orders/{order_id}/invoice")
async def invoice(order_id: int) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A failure nobody handled: the client gets a bare 500 with the request ID to quote, and the
    server logs the traceback under that ID."""
    raise ConnectionError(f"pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order {order_id}")


@router.get("/reports/sales")
async def sales_report(db: DB) -> dict[str, int]:
    """At the deadline the query is cancelled, the connection goes back to the pool and the
    client gets a 504, instead of both waiting for as long as the query takes."""
    await asyncio.sleep(db.report_seconds)
    return {"orders": len(db.orders)}


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


def create_app(*, request_timeout: float = 10.0) -> FastAPI:
    """The application, with a deadline of `request_timeout` seconds per request."""
    application = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
    # In memory: nothing but this process reads or writes it. Alcazaba's metrics are recorded
    # through it, and /health/ready checks it.
    Cache(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="orders").install(application)
    FastAPIProblemDetails().install(application)
    application.include_router(router)

    async def database() -> None:
        await application.state.db.ping()

    application.include_router(health_router({"database": database}))
    # The last middleware added is the outermost. RequestIDMiddleware goes around the deadline, so
    # that the 504 it answers carries the ID too. (A 500 is answered outside every middleware;
    # FastAPIProblemDetails adds the ID to it itself.)
    application.add_middleware(
        RequestTimeoutMiddleware,
        timeout=request_timeout,
        paths={"/orders/export": None},
    )
    # Keeps a safe X-Request-ID set by the proxy (or the client); trust_incoming=False if clients
    # reach the application directly and shouldn't choose their IDs.
    application.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)
    return application


app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True, log_config=LOGGING)

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operations Admin to Your app: PUT /admin/maintenance. Users to Your app: GET /checkout. Your app to Users: 503, Retry-After: 900. Admin to Your app: DELETE /admin/maintenance. Admin to Your app: new-checkout: 30 %. Users to Your app: GET /checkout. Your app: is the user in the 30 %? Your app to Users: 200, new or classic. Close, reopen and roll out at runtime, without a deploy. Users Your app Admin PUT /admin/maintenance GET /checkout 503, Retry-After: 900 DELETE /admin/maintenance new-checkout: 30 % GET /checkout is the user in the 30 %? 200, new or classic Close, reopen and roll out at runtime, without a deploy What it's for: switches flipped at runtime, without a deploy: maintenance mode, features rolled out to some of the users, and a breaker for a service that's down.

An app operated at runtime, without a deploy, through a small admin API that takes a bearer token. It closes and reopens the app with FastAPIMaintenance, whose middleware answers 503 with Retry-After to everything but the health check and the admin routes. It defines FastAPIFeatureFlags: a new checkout rolled out to a percentage of the users, and a beta page that only the users on an allow list can see (a 404 for everybody else). And a FastAPIBreaker turns the failures of a flaky shipping service into a fast 503 while it's down.

The maintenance switch and the flags live in the backend, so a change made through one process reaches all of them. Each process keeps a copy for up to 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags), so that requests don't each ask the backend. The breaker is each process's own.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.operations.main:app

The admin routes take Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN. Set ADMIN_TOKEN and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without ADMIN_TOKEN, the app makes one up at each start and logs it:

ADMIN_TOKEN isn't set: the admin token of this run is YbLt_8-WKnm4zWknL3mgHNar4E3MmBsCNtk6KPJLBB4

It keeps the switch and the flags in memory, so don't start it with --workers: each worker would have a switch of its own. In production, a Redis or Valkey backend lets every process share them.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
$ TOKEN=YbLt_8-WKnm4zWknL3mgHNar4E3MmBsCNtk6KPJLBB4

Without the token, the admin routes answer 401:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Unauthorized"}

Close the app for maintenance. Every request gets a 503 with the message and Retry-After, but the health check is still served:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Back at 10:30", "retry_after": 900}'
{"enabled":true,"message":"Back at 10:30","retry_after":900,"since":1793011967.4372241}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
cache-control: no-store
retry-after: 900

{"detail": "Back at 10:30"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
{"status":"ok"}

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
{"checkout":"classic"}

Roll the new checkout out to 30 % of the users. Here the bearer token stands for the user, so that you can try it with curl. Each user keeps their answer from one request to the next, and anonymous visitors aren't part of a partial rollout:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/flags/new-checkout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled": true, "percentage": 30}'
{"name":"new-checkout","enabled":true,"percentage":30.0,"allow":[],"deny":[]}

$ for user in ana bea carlos david elena; do \
    echo "$user: $(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout -H "Authorization: Bearer $user")"; \
  done
ana: {"checkout":"new"}
bea: {"checkout":"classic"}
carlos: {"checkout":"classic"}
david: {"checkout":"new"}
elena: {"checkout":"classic"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
{"checkout":"classic"}

The beta report is a 404, like a page that doesn't exist, until the user is on the allow list. Without a percentage, a flag with an allow list is for nobody else. The list comes back as digests: the backend never gets the users' ids.

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer ana"
{"detail":"Not Found"}

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/flags/beta-reports -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled": true, "allow": ["ana"]}'
{"name":"beta-reports","enabled":true,"percentage":null,"allow":["44d27c2ae32d479abf13f231ea9ee8295988d4a14fdf8be30c16aa81e894946b"],"deny":[]}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer ana"
{"report":"Sales by hour"}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer bea"
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found

{"detail":"Not Found"}

Make the shipping service fail. The first three requests wait for it and get a 502; then the breaker opens, and requests get a 503 at once, without calling the service:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/shipping?down=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping    # three times
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

{"detail":"The shipping service failed"}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
retry-after: 30

{"detail":"Service Unavailable"}

The status page reads the shared state from the backend, and the breaker from this process:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/status -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"maintenance":{"enabled":false,"message":null,"retry_after":null,"since":null},"flags":{"new-checkout":{...},"beta-reports":{...}},"process":{"pid":831700,"shipping_breaker":"open"}}

The breaker stays open for 30 s, even when the service is back. Then a single request tries it, and its success closes the breaker:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/shipping?down=false" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
retry-after: 30

{"detail":"Service Unavailable"}

$ sleep 30; curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

Or, once you know the service is back, close the breaker at once. Only in the process that gets the request: each process has its own.

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/breakers/shipping/close -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The admin token is compared in constant time, as bytes: secrets.compare_digest takes the same time however much of a guess is right. It compares bytes because on strings it raises when a client sends non-ASCII characters: a 500 instead of a 401.
  • Shared state, local copies: the switch and the flags are in the backend, signed with CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, so a state planted there by someone else is ignored. Each process reads them again at most every refresh seconds, so a change takes up to 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags) to reach the other processes; the process that made it, and /admin/status, see it at once. The breaker is created in the lifespan, one per process: it opens after that process's failures, with no round trip on every call.
  • /health and /admin are always served: the orchestrator doesn't restart processes that are only in maintenance, and the API that closed the app can reopen it.
  • Flag names are an enum: no flag the app never reads can be created. A flag with an allow list and no percentage is only for the list, so a beta never goes to everyone by mistake.
  • Subjects come from authentication: a route hidden by flags.require() takes its subject from a function of the request. Here the bearer token is the user id; in a real app take it from a session or a token you verify, or anyone could put themselves on an allow list.
  • Only what says the service is down opens the breaker: failures=(ConnectionError,), so a bug of ours doesn't, and a call that hangs is cancelled after 5 s and counts too. A failure is a 502; a refusal while the breaker is open, a 503 with Retry-After.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/operations/main.py
"""Operating an app without a deploy: maintenance mode, feature flags and a circuit breaker.

    uvicorn examples.operations.main:app

- `PUT /admin/maintenance` closes the app: a 503 with `Retry-After` for every request but
  `/health` (the load balancer keeps the processes) and `/admin` (you can reopen it).
- `PUT /admin/flags/{name}`: `new-checkout` goes to a percentage of the users, always the same
  ones; `/reports/beta` is a 404 but for the users on the allow list of `beta-reports`.
- `/orders/{order_id}/shipping` calls a flaky shipping service (simulated). After 3 failures in a
  row, each a 502 that waited for it, the breaker opens: a 503 at once for 30 s, without calling
  it. Then one request tries again; `POST /admin/breakers/shipping/close` closes it at once.

The admin routes take `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.

The maintenance switch and the flags live in the backend, shared by every process. Each process
keeps a copy, read again at most every 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags): requests don't each ask
the backend, and a change reaches every process within that. Breakers are each process's own:
one opens after its process's failures, with no round trip on every call.
"""

import logging
import os
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import (
    BackendUnavailable,
    FastAPIBreaker,
    FastAPICache,
    FastAPIFeatureFlags,
    FastAPIMaintenance,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.operations import MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH, FeatureFlag, MaintenanceMiddleware
from fastapi_alcazaba.operations.maintenance import MaintenanceStatus

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file. Set both in production, the
    same in every process (secrets.token_urlsafe(32))."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    admin_token: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    # Seals the switch and the flags in the backend: a state planted there by someone else is
    # ignored, and so is what a process with another key writes.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Flag(StrEnum):
    """The flags this app reads: the admin routes define only these."""

    NEW_CHECKOUT = "new-checkout"
    BETA_REPORTS = "beta-reports"


class Quote(BaseModel):
    order_id: int
    carrier: str
    days: int


class ShippingService:
    """Stands in for a downstream service and its SDK: fails while `down`, and counts the calls
    that reach it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.down = False
        self.calls = 0

    async def quote(self, order_id: int) -> Quote:
        self.calls += 1
        if self.down:
            raise ConnectionError("the shipping service doesn't answer")
        return Quote(order_id=order_id, carrier="Alhambra Express", days=2)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the switch and the flags:
    # InMemoryBackend keeps them in this process.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="ops", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    application.state.shipping = ShippingService()
    # Only what says the service is down counts, not a bug of ours; a call that hangs is cancelled
    # after 5 s and counts too.
    application.state.shipping_breaker = FastAPIBreaker(
        "shipping", failure_threshold=3, reset_timeout=30, timeout=5, failures=(ConnectionError,)
    )
    if "admin_token" not in settings.model_fields_set:
        token = settings.admin_token.get_secret_value()
        logger.warning("ADMIN_TOKEN isn't set: the admin token of this run is %s", token)
    yield


# How old each process's copy of the shared state may be, in seconds.
maintenance = FastAPIMaintenance(refresh=1)
flags = FastAPIFeatureFlags(refresh=5)

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(
    MaintenanceMiddleware, maintenance=maintenance, allow_paths=("/health", "/admin")
)


@app.exception_handler(BackendUnavailable)
async def backend_unavailable(_request: Request, _exc: BackendUnavailable) -> JSONResponse:
    """An admin change the backend didn't take: nothing changed, and the response says so."""
    return JSONResponse({"detail": "Not changed: the backend is unavailable"}, status_code=503)


def current_user(connection: HTTPConnection) -> str | None:
    """The user's id. Stands in for your authentication: here the bearer token is the id itself,
    so that you can try it with curl. Take it from a session or a token you verify, or anyone
    could put themselves on an allow list."""
    scheme, _, token = connection.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    return token if scheme.lower() == "bearer" and token else None


@app.get("/health")
async def health() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Served during maintenance too: the processes are fine, nothing should restart them."""
    return {"status": "ok"}


@app.get("/checkout")
async def checkout(user: Annotated[str | None, Depends(current_user)]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The new checkout for the users in the rollout; without a user, a partial rollout is off."""
    new = await flags.enabled(Flag.NEW_CHECKOUT, subject=user)
    return {"checkout": "new" if new else "classic"}


@app.get(
    "/reports/beta",
    dependencies=[Depends(flags.require(Flag.BETA_REPORTS, subject=current_user))],
)
async def beta_report() -> dict[str, str]:
    """A 404 for the users the flag is off for, as if the route didn't exist."""
    return {"report": "Sales by hour"}


@app.get("/orders/{order_id}/shipping")
async def shipping_quote(order_id: int, request: Request) -> Quote:
    """A 502 when the service fails; while the breaker is open, a 503 with Retry-After."""
    breaker: FastAPIBreaker = request.app.state.shipping_breaker
    shipping: ShippingService = request.app.state.shipping
    try:
        async with breaker.attempt():
            return await shipping.quote(order_id)
    except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError) as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_502_BAD_GATEWAY, "The shipping service failed") from exc


def require_admin(
    credentials: Annotated[
        HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(HTTPBearer(auto_error=False))
    ],
) -> None:
    """Compared in constant time, and as bytes: compare_digest refuses strings with non-ASCII
    characters, which a client can send."""
    token = credentials.credentials if credentials is not None else ""
    if not secrets.compare_digest(token.encode(), settings.admin_token.get_secret_value().encode()):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})


admin = APIRouter(prefix="/admin", dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])


class MaintenanceUpdate(BaseModel):
    message: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH)
    retry_after: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)


class FlagUpdate(BaseModel):
    enabled: bool
    # None: everybody, or only the allow list when there's one.
    percentage: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)
    allow: list[str] = Field(default=[], max_length=1000)
    deny: list[str] = Field(default=[], max_length=1000)


@admin.put("/maintenance")
async def start_maintenance(update: MaintenanceUpdate) -> MaintenanceStatus:
    """Close the app, in every process within a second."""
    return await maintenance.enable(update.message, update.retry_after)


@admin.delete("/maintenance", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def end_maintenance() -> None:
    await maintenance.disable()


@admin.put("/flags/{name}")
async def set_flag(name: Flag, update: FlagUpdate) -> FeatureFlag:
    """Define a flag, for every process within 5 seconds. The lists come back as digests: the
    backend never gets the users' ids."""
    return await flags.set(name, **update.model_dump())


@admin.put("/simulate/shipping", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def simulate_shipping(down: bool, request: Request) -> None:
    """Only in this example: makes the shipping service fail, to watch the breaker open."""
    request.app.state.shipping.down = down


@admin.post("/breakers/shipping/close", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def close_shipping_breaker(request: Request) -> None:
    """The shipping service is back: call it again now, instead of waiting for the trial. Only
    in the process that gets this request: each process has its own breaker."""
    request.app.state.shipping_breaker.reset()


@admin.get("/status")
async def status_report(request: Request) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The shared state as the backend has it now (this process's copies are updated with it),
    and the breaker as this process sees it."""
    breaker: FastAPIBreaker = request.app.state.shipping_breaker
    return {
        "maintenance": await maintenance.status(),
        "flags": {flag: await flags.get(flag) for flag in Flag},
        "process": {"pid": os.getpid(), "shipping_breaker": breaker.state},
    }


app.include_router(admin)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Checking uploads
docs.text:
Checking uploads User to Your app: POST /avatars, cat.png. Your app: ✓ a PNG, by its bytes. Your app to Storage: stored as <uuid>.png. Your app to User: 201 Created. User to Your app: cat.html, named cat.png. Your app: ✗ HTML, whatever its name. Your app to User: 415 Unsupported Media Type. Judged by their bytes, stored under names of the app's own. User Your app Storage POST /avatars, cat.png ✓ a PNG, by its bytes stored as <uuid>.png 201 Created cat.html, named cat.png ✗ HTML, whatever its name 415 Unsupported Media Type Judged by their bytes, stored under names of the app's own What it's for: files judged by what they are, not by the name or type the client gives, before the app stores them or serves them back.

An app where users upload an avatar and documents, then download them again. Every file is judged by its bytes, not by its name or the Content-Type the client sent: FastAPIUploads checks avatars (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MiB and 16 million pixels) as a dependency, and documents (PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, up to five at a time) with check(). Files are stored under names of the app's own and served back with the type found in them.

BodySizeLimitMiddleware gives each route a body limit, and SecurityHeadersMiddleware adds X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff to every response, so browsers don't second-guess the type.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.uploads.main:app

Files go to a temporary directory, deleted at shutdown; set UPLOAD_DIR to keep them.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
An image is stored, with the type and dimensions read from its bytes:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/avatars -F file=@cat.png
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json
x-content-type-options: nosniff

{"id":"6b88b761-8ff4-4477-bc9e-568420bd4205","name":"cat.png","content_type":"image/png","size":179,"width":64,"height":64}

An HTML page sent as cat.png, with Content-Type: image/png, is refused. Served back as it was declared, it would run its script in the browser:

$ printf '<!doctype html><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>' > cat.html
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/avatars -F 'file=@cat.html;filename=cat.png;type=image/png'
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type

{"detail":"Unsupported file type"}

A PNG of 33 bytes whose header says 50,000 × 50,000 pixels would take gigabytes of memory to decode. Its dimensions are read from the header, without decoding it:

$ python -c "import struct, sys, zlib; h = b'IHDR' + struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', 50000, 50000, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0); sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + struct.pack('>I', 13) + h + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(h)))" > bomb.png
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/avatars -F file=@bomb.png
HTTP/1.1 413 Content Too Large

{"detail":"Image too large"}

A body over the route's limit is refused from its Content-Length, before the multipart parser stores it:

$ head -c 3145728 /dev/urandom > big.jpg
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/avatars -F file=@big.jpg
HTTP/1.1 413 Content Too Large
x-content-type-options: nosniff

{"detail":"Request body too large"}

Several documents at once. The second is a Word document named minutes.pdf: it's stored as what it is.

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents -F files=@invoice.pdf -F 'files=@minutes.docx;filename=minutes.pdf'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

[{"id":"1f8b5cef-0d26-48e2-b6d0-03cdd086c6f0","name":"invoice.pdf","content_type":"application/pdf","size":142,"width":null,"height":null},{"id":"5a667cf4-565c-4e7a-88ef-ae6a014c1761","name":"minutes.pdf","content_type":"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document","size":540,"width":null,"height":null}]

And it's served as a Word document, as an attachment, with the extension that says so:

$ curl -D - -o minutes.docx http://127.0.0.1:8000/files/5a667cf4-565c-4e7a-88ef-ae6a014c1761
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document
content-disposition: attachment; filename="minutes.docx"
content-length: 540
x-content-type-options: nosniff
content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The type comes from the bytes: CheckedFile.content_type is what the file is, whatever its name or the client's Content-Type. It's stored with the file and used to serve it, together with nosniff, so a browser can't be talked into reading an upload as HTML.
  • Names of the app's own: each file is stored as {uuid}{CheckedFile.extension}. The client's name (CheckedFile.filename, already made safe) is kept for display, and the download name goes through safe_filename again with the real extension: no path, no control or invisible characters (such as the right-to-left override), _ before the names Windows reserves.
  • Two size limits, on purpose: the multipart parser stores the whole request before an endpoint runs, so BodySizeLimitMiddleware bounds it per route (a little more than the files allowed, for the multipart framing; 64 KiB anywhere else). FastAPIUploads then counts each file exactly, and checks the pixels of images.
  • All or nothing: /documents checks every file before it stores any, so one bad file in a request leaves nothing half-saved.
  • Attachments for documents: a PDF can carry scripts, so documents are downloaded rather than opened by the browser; images are shown inline.
  • SecurityHeadersMiddleware last: added last, it's the outermost middleware, so the 413s of BodySizeLimitMiddleware get the security headers too.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/uploads/main.py
"""Avatars and documents uploaded, checked by their bytes, stored and served back safely.

    uvicorn examples.uploads.main:app

- `POST /avatars`: one image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) of up to 2 MiB and 16 million pixels,
  checked by `FastAPIUploads` as a dependency.
- `POST /documents`: up to five PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint files of up to 10 MiB each, all
  checked with `check()` before any of them is stored.
- `GET /files/{file_id}`: a file back, with the type found in its bytes, never the one the
  client said, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Images inline; documents as attachments,
  under the client's name made safe, with the extension of what the file really is.

A file is judged by its bytes, not by its name or `Content-Type`: an HTML page sent as `cat.png`
gets a 415. Files are stored under names of the app's own. `BodySizeLimitMiddleware` gives each
route a limit, so that the multipart parser doesn't store a huge body before the checks run.
"""

import shutil
import tempfile
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import ExitStack, asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, BinaryIO
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, File, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile, status
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool

from fastapi_alcazaba.security import BodySizeLimitMiddleware, SecurityHeadersMiddleware
from fastapi_alcazaba.uploads import IMAGES, CheckedFile, FastAPIUploads, safe_filename
from fastapi_alcazaba.uploads.checks import OFFICE_DOCUMENTS

MIB = 1024 * 1024
MAX_DOCUMENTS = 5
avatars = FastAPIUploads(types=IMAGES, max_size=2 * MIB, max_pixels=16_000_000)
# Without the macro-enabled Office types (.docm, .xlsm, .pptm): OFFICE_DOCUMENTS leaves them out.
documents = FastAPIUploads(types={"application/pdf", *OFFICE_DOCUMENTS}, max_size=10 * MIB)


class StoredFile(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    key: str = Field(exclude=True)  # where it's stored: its id and the extension of its type
    name: str  # the client's, made safe: for display only
    content_type: str  # found in its bytes
    size: int
    width: int | None = None
    height: int | None = None


class Storage:
    """Files in a directory, under names of the app's own. Their details are kept in memory,
    where a real app has a database table (and maybe object storage, such as S3, for the
    files)."""

    def __init__(self, directory: Path) -> None:
        self.directory = directory
        self.files: dict[UUID, StoredFile] = {}

    async def save(self, upload: CheckedFile) -> StoredFile:
        file_id = uuid4()
        stored = StoredFile(
            id=file_id,
            key=f"{file_id}{upload.extension}",  # never the client's name
            name=upload.filename,
            content_type=upload.content_type,
            size=upload.size,
            width=upload.width,
            height=upload.height,
        )
        await run_in_threadpool(self._write, self.directory / stored.key, upload.file.file)
        self.files[file_id] = stored
        return stored

    @staticmethod
    def _write(path: Path, source: BinaryIO) -> None:
        with path.open("xb") as target:  # "x": never overwrite a file
            shutil.copyfileobj(source, target)


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    upload_dir: Path | None = None


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    with ExitStack() as stack:
        # UPLOAD_DIR in production: a volume that every process shares. For local development, a
        # throwaway directory, deleted at shutdown.
        directory = Settings().upload_dir or stack.enter_context(
            tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="uploads-")
        )
        application.state.storage = Storage(Path(directory))
        yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
# Uploads only where they're expected, with room for the multipart framing around the files.
app.add_middleware(
    BodySizeLimitMiddleware,
    max_size=64 * 1024,
    paths={"/avatars": 2 * MIB + 16 * 1024, "/documents": MAX_DOCUMENTS * 10 * MIB + 64 * 1024},
)
app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)  # last, the outermost: the 413s get the headers too


def get_storage(request: Request) -> Storage:
    storage: Storage = request.app.state.storage
    return storage


StorageDep = Annotated[Storage, Depends(get_storage)]


@app.post("/avatars", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def upload_avatar(
    upload: Annotated[CheckedFile, Depends(avatars)],
    storage: StorageDep,
) -> StoredFile:
    """One image, in the form field `file`: 415 if it isn't one, 413 if it's too large."""
    return await storage.save(upload)


@app.post("/documents", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def upload_documents(
    files: Annotated[list[UploadFile], File()],
    storage: StorageDep,
) -> list[StoredFile]:
    """Several documents, in the form field `files`: all checked before any is stored, so that
    one bad file stores none."""
    if len(files) > MAX_DOCUMENTS:
        raise HTTPException(422, f"At most {MAX_DOCUMENTS} files at a time")
    checked = [await documents.check(file) for file in files]
    return [await storage.save(upload) for upload in checked]


@app.get("/files/{file_id}")
async def download(file_id: UUID, storage: StorageDep) -> FileResponse:
    """The file, as the type found in its bytes. A real app checks who may read it."""
    stored = storage.files.get(file_id)
    if stored is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "File not found")
    # The client's name with the extension of the real type: a Word document sent as
    # `minutes.pdf` is downloaded as `minutes.docx`, and opens in the right program.
    stem = stored.name.rpartition(".")[0] or stored.name
    return FileResponse(
        storage.directory / stored.key,
        media_type=stored.content_type,
        filename=safe_filename(stem + Path(stored.key).suffix),
        # A PDF can carry scripts: the browser saves documents rather than open them.
        content_disposition_type="inline" if stored.content_type in IMAGES else "attachment",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Webhooks in and out
docs.text:
Webhooks in and out Payment provider to Your shop: POST /webhooks/payments. Your shop: ✓ signature, fresh, new. Your shop to Payment provider: 204. Payment provider to Your shop: the same delivery again. Your shop to Payment provider: 401, seen already. Your shop to User's endpoint: order.paid, signed. User's endpoint to Your shop: 200. Signed webhooks in, each once; signed webhooks out. Payment provider Your shop User's endpoint POST /webhooks/payments ✓ signature, fresh, new 204 the same delivery again 401, seen already order.paid, signed 200 Signed webhooks in, each once; signed webhooks out What it's for: webhooks taken only when signed with the sender's secret, each delivery once, and webhooks sent signed, to URLs that can't reach the app's own network.

A shop that takes webhooks from its payment provider and sends webhooks of its own to the URLs its users register. FastAPIWebhooks accepts only the provider's events signed with its secret, and each delivery once. When an order is paid, the shop signs an order.paid event with each user's secret (WebhookSigner) and sends it through ResilientTransport, for a deadline and a circuit breaker per endpoint, around SSRFGuardTransport, so that a user can't point the shop at its own network.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET=$(python -c "from fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks import WebhookSigner; print(WebhookSigner.generate_secret())")
uvicorn examples.webhooks.main:app

In production, the provider gives the secret when you set up the endpoint. Without PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET the app makes a throwaway one, which nobody else can sign with.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
A request without a signature:

$ BODY='{"type": "payment.succeeded", "data": {"order_id": "ord_1", "amount": 1999}}'
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/webhooks/payments -d "$BODY"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"Invalid webhook"}

Sign it as the provider would, with the same secret (in the same shell as the export), and keep the headers in a file for curl:

$ sign() { python -c 'import os, sys; from fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks import WebhookSigner; \
    signer = WebhookSigner(os.environ["PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]); \
    headers = signer.sign(sys.argv[1], message_id="msg_1"); \
    print("\n".join(f"{name}: {value}" for name, value in headers.items()))' "$BODY" > signed.txt; }
$ sign && cat signed.txt
webhook-id: msg_1
webhook-timestamp: 1793012100
webhook-signature: v1,r/kZwT7lk1Z+roS1OQd6pcxNinGLv8NUwlkJ964CYK0=
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/webhooks/payments -H @signed.txt -d "$BODY"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

The same request again, as someone who captured it would send it, and the same signature on another body:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/webhooks/payments -H @signed.txt -d "$BODY"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

{"detail":"Invalid webhook"}
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/webhooks/payments -H @signed.txt -d "${BODY/1999/1}"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

{"detail":"Invalid webhook"}

A retry of the provider has the same webhook-id and a new timestamp and signature. It goes through, and the handler, which has seen msg_1 already, does nothing:

$ sign && curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/webhooks/payments -H @signed.txt -d "$BODY"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

Registering an endpoint sends it a signed ping. A URL that isn't on the public internet is refused before anything is sent: the cloud's metadata service, which hands out credentials, the server itself, or a port other than 80 and 443:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/endpoints -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"url": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content

{"detail":"Not allowed: http://169.254.169.254: its address isn't allowed"}
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/endpoints -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"url": "http://localhost/admin"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content

{"detail":"Not allowed: http://localhost: its address isn't allowed"}
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/endpoints -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"url": "http://localhost:6379/"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content

{"detail":"Not allowed: http://localhost:6379: port 6379 isn't allowed"}

A public URL that answers the ping with a 2xx is registered, and the answer carries its secret (whsec_...), shown once. Its deliveries are listed at /endpoints/{id}/deliveries.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The signature is checked before the body is parsed: the endpoint takes the WebhookMessage and validates message.body itself. A pydantic body parameter would make FastAPI read and parse the whole body before the dependency runs, signed or not.
  • Replays and retries are different things: FastAPIWebhooks refuses a delivery it has seen (same id and timestamp), in every process that shares the backend. A retry is a new delivery of the same message, so the handler is idempotent on message.id: in a database, a unique constraint on a row written in the same transaction as the order.
  • One secret per endpoint: each user gets their own, made by WebhookSigner.generate_secret(), so one leaked secret doesn't forge events for the others. The exact bytes sent are the ones signed, and every attempt of an event keeps its id.
  • Checked when sent, not only when registered: SSRFGuardTransport resolves the host on every call and connects to the address it checked, so a name that later points to 10.0.0.7 (or answers DNS differently the second time) gets a blocked delivery, not a request to the private network.
  • The guard inside ResilientTransport: the 10-second deadline covers the DNS lookup, and each origin (scheme, host and port) has its own breaker: after five failures in a row it's skipped for a minute instead of being waited for. Responses are read up to 64 KiB, and redirects aren't followed.
  • After the response: deliveries run as a background task, all endpoints at once, so the provider gets its 204 without waiting for the users' servers. A real app hands them to a task queue that retries failures.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/webhooks/main.py
"""A shop that receives signed webhooks from its payment provider, and sends signed webhooks to
the URLs its users register.

    export PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...  # the provider's secret for this endpoint
    uvicorn examples.webhooks.main:app

- `POST /webhooks/payments`: the provider's events, signed, recent and each delivery once
  (`FastAPIWebhooks`): a captured request sent again gets a 401. The provider's retries keep the
  `webhook-id`, so the handler is idempotent on it.
- `POST /endpoints`: a user registers a URL and gets the secret to check the shop's events with.
  A signed `ping` goes there first, through `SSRFGuardTransport`: a URL that isn't on the public
  internet (`http://169.254.169.254/`, `http://localhost`, a private network) gets a 422.
- When an order is paid, every endpoint gets a signed `order.paid` event after the response,
  through `ResilientTransport`: a deadline for each call and a circuit breaker for each endpoint.

Replays are remembered in the cache's backend: InMemoryBackend here, Redis or Valkey in
production, so that every process refuses them.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Annotated, Any

import httpx2 as httpx
import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, BackgroundTasks, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, HttpUrl, SecretStr, ValidationError
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.outbound import (
    BlockedDestinationError,
    CircuitOpenError,
    ResilientTransport,
    SSRFGuardTransport,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks import FastAPIWebhooks, WebhookMessage, WebhookSigner


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    # The provider gives it when the endpoint is set up. Without it, a throwaway one for local
    # development, which nobody else can sign with.
    payments_webhook_secret: SecretStr = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: SecretStr(WebhookSigner.generate_secret())
    )


settings = Settings()
payment_webhooks = FastAPIWebhooks(settings.payments_webhook_secret)


class Payment(BaseModel):
    order_id: str
    amount: int  # in cents


class PaymentEvent(BaseModel):
    type: str  # payment.succeeded, payment.failed...
    data: Payment


class NewEndpoint(BaseModel):
    url: HttpUrl


class CreatedEndpoint(BaseModel):
    id: str
    url: str
    secret: str  # shown once: the user checks the shop's signatures with it


class Delivery(BaseModel):
    event_id: str
    type: str
    outcome: str


@dataclass
class Endpoint:
    """A user's URL. A real database keeps its secret encrypted."""

    id: str
    url: str
    signer: WebhookSigner
    deliveries: list[Delivery] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class Shop:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    paid: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # The provider's messages handled already: a unique constraint in a database, on a row
    # inserted in the same transaction as their effects.
    handled: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    endpoints: dict[str, Endpoint] = field(default_factory=dict)


def get_shop(request: Request) -> Shop:
    shop: Shop = request.app.state.shop
    return shop


def get_client(request: Request) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    client: httpx.AsyncClient = request.app.state.client
    return client


ShopDep = Annotated[Shop, Depends(get_shop)]
ClientDep = Annotated[httpx.AsyncClient, Depends(get_client)]
router = APIRouter()


async def post_event(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient,
    endpoint: Endpoint,
    event: dict[str, Any],
) -> httpx.Response:
    body = json.dumps(event).encode()  # signed as sent: json= would serialise it again
    headers = endpoint.signer.sign(body, message_id=event["id"])  # the same id on every retry
    headers["content-type"] = "application/json"
    return await client.post(endpoint.url, content=body, headers=headers)


async def deliver(client: httpx.AsyncClient, endpoint: Endpoint, event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Send `event` and log what happened. A real app retries failed deliveries later, from a
    task queue, with the same event id."""
    try:
        response = await post_event(client, endpoint, event)
        outcome = "delivered" if response.is_success else f"HTTP {response.status_code}"
    except CircuitOpenError:
        outcome = "skipped"  # it failed too often lately: not called for a minute
    except BlockedDestinationError:
        outcome = "blocked"  # its name points to a private address now
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:  # can't connect, no answer in time, answer too large...
        outcome = type(exc).__name__
    endpoint.deliveries.append(Delivery(event_id=event["id"], type=event["type"], outcome=outcome))


async def notify(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient,
    endpoints: list[Endpoint],
    event: dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Send `event` to every endpoint at once: they don't wait for each other."""
    await asyncio.gather(*(deliver(client, endpoint, event) for endpoint in endpoints))


@router.post("/webhooks/payments", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def payment_event(
    message: Annotated[WebhookMessage, Depends(payment_webhooks)],
    shop: ShopDep,
    client: ClientDep,
    background: BackgroundTasks,
) -> None:
    """The provider's events. Every attempt of a message has the same id: the first one does the
    work, the others only get their 204."""
    if message.id in shop.handled:
        return
    # Parsed once its signature is checked: FastAPI would parse a body parameter before.
    try:
        event = PaymentEvent.model_validate_json(message.body)
    except ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(422, "Not a payment event") from None
    shop.handled.add(message.id)
    if event.type == "payment.succeeded":
        shop.paid[event.data.order_id] = event.data.amount
        order_paid = {"id": f"evt_{secrets.token_hex(12)}", "type": "order.paid"}
        # After the response: the provider doesn't wait for the users' servers.
        background.add_task(
            notify, client, list(shop.endpoints.values()), order_paid | event.data.model_dump()
        )


@router.post("/endpoints", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_endpoint(new: NewEndpoint, shop: ShopDep, client: ClientDep) -> CreatedEndpoint:
    """Register a URL for the shop's events, if it accepts a signed ping. A real app keeps each
    user's endpoints apart."""
    secret = WebhookSigner.generate_secret()
    endpoint = Endpoint(f"ep_{secrets.token_hex(8)}", str(new.url), WebhookSigner(secret))
    ping = {"id": f"evt_{secrets.token_hex(12)}", "type": "ping"}
    try:
        response = await post_event(client, endpoint, ping)
    except BlockedDestinationError as exc:  # says which host, never the address it resolved to
        raise HTTPException(422, f"Not allowed: {exc}") from None
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(422, f"The ping failed: {type(exc).__name__}") from None
    if not response.is_success:
        raise HTTPException(422, f"The ping got HTTP {response.status_code}")
    shop.endpoints[endpoint.id] = endpoint
    return CreatedEndpoint(id=endpoint.id, url=endpoint.url, secret=secret)


@router.get("/endpoints/{endpoint_id}/deliveries")
async def deliveries(endpoint_id: str, shop: ShopDep) -> list[Delivery]:
    endpoint = shop.endpoints.get(endpoint_id)
    if endpoint is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "Endpoint not found")
    return endpoint.deliveries


def create_app(transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    """The application. `transport` sends the outgoing requests once they're checked: the network by
    default, a mock in tests."""

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process refuses a replay. The marks are
        # counters, which a signing_key doesn't cover: keep the backend out of others' reach.
        FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
        # Only public addresses, on the web's ports, checked again on every call.
        guard = SSRFGuardTransport(transport, ports=(80, 443))
        outbound = ResilientTransport(
            guard, timeout=10, failure_threshold=5, reset_timeout=60, max_response_size=65_536
        )
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=outbound) as client:  # it follows no redirects
            application.state.client = client
            application.state.shop = Shop()
            yield

    application = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
    application.include_router(router)
    return application


app = create_app()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Authentication strategies
docs.text:
One route, several strategies Browser to Your app: GET /me, Cookie: session. Your app: "session" ✓. Your app to Browser: 200 octocat. Script to Your app: GET /me, Bearer eyJ… Your app: "session" ✗ → "jwt" ✓. Your app to Script: 200 octocat. auth.authenticate("session", "jwt"): the first that finds the user. Browser Your app Script GET /me, Cookie: session "session" ✓ 200 octocat GET /me, Bearer eyJ… "session" ✗ → "jwt" ✓ 200 octocat auth.authenticate("session", "jwt"): the first that finds the user What it's for: one route that browsers reach with their session and scripts with a token, each strategy tried in order.

Each strategy has an example of its own, a small app to run and try:

  • JWTStrategy: scripts log in with a password and send a JWT, which they can revoke.
  • OAuth2Strategy: people log in with their GitHub account.
  • SessionStrategy: a password, then a session that remembers who logged in.
  • HTTPBearerStrategy: personal access tokens, refused as soon as they're deleted.
  • SAMLStrategy: single sign-on with a SAML identity provider.
  • Your own strategy: API keys in X-API-Key.

This one puts three strategies together. People log in with their GitHub account; their scripts, with tokens they create. OAuth2Strategy logs people in with GitHub, SessionStrategy remembers them in a server-side session afterwards, and JWTStrategy reads the tokens of their scripts. /me takes the last two: auth.authenticate("session", "jwt") tries them in order.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Create a GitHub OAuth app (GitHub's Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps) whose callback URL is http://localhost:8000/auth/github/callback. Then, from a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=... GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=...
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.main:app

Set JWT_SECRET and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process. Without them each start makes up throwaway ones, and the sessions and tokens stop working when the app restarts. Open the app at http://localhost:8000, not 127.0.0.1: GitHub only sends people back to the callback URL it knows.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Without a session or a token, nobody:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Open http://localhost:8000/login/github in the browser and log in with GitHub, as in the OAuth2 example: the app starts a session and takes you to /me. For a GitHub user called octocat:

{"id":"github:583231","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

In the same browser, open http://localhost:8000/docs and try POST /tokens: it makes a token for your scripts, valid for an hour:

{"access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJnaXRodWI6NTgzMjMxIi...","token_type":"bearer","expires_in":3600}

A script uses it instead of the session:

$ TOKEN=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJnaXRodWI6NTgzMjMxIi...
$ curl http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"id":"github:583231","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

But it can't make tokens: /tokens only takes the session, so a leaked token can't make more. With only the session strategy tried, the 401 has no challenge:

$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8000/tokens -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

The script can revoke its token, which is refused from then on, until it would have expired:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/tokens/current -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• One dependency per way in: GitHubUser, SessionUser, TokenUser and AnyUser say which strategies each route accepts. The callback only takes GitHub's answer, /tokens only a session, /me a session or a token.
  • In order: AnyUser tries the session first, then the token. A strategy that finds nothing of its own in the request (no cookie, no Authorization) passes to the next one; when none finds a user, the 401 carries the challenges of those tried.
  • The app owns its users: find_or_create_user turns GitHub's profile into a user of the app, created the first time. Sessions and tokens carry the app's user id, never GitHub's token.
  • CSRF: the session is a cookie, which browsers send by themselves; CSRFMiddleware refuses what other sites make them send. Requests with a token aren't checked: only the app's pages (or a script) can add an Authorization header.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/main.py
"""People log in with GitHub; their scripts, with tokens they create: authentication strategies.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.main:app

Three strategies, each a way to tell who makes a request: `OAuth2Strategy` logs people in with
their GitHub account, `SessionStrategy` remembers them in a server-side session afterwards, and
`JWTStrategy` reads the tokens they create for their scripts. `/me` takes any of the last two:
`auth.authenticate("session", "jwt")` tries them in order.

Create a GitHub OAuth app (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps) whose callback URL is
http://localhost:8000/auth/github/callback, and set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET.
Set JWT_SECRET and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every
process, in the environment or a .env file. Open the app at http://localhost:8000: GitHub only
sends people back to the callback URL it knows.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import SessionStrategy, TokenBlocklist
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.jwt import JWTStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.oauth2 import OAuth2Strategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.security import CSRFMiddleware, ServerSessionMiddleware

TOKEN_LIFETIME = 3600  # seconds


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"
    github_client_id: str = "set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"
    github_client_secret: SecretStr = SecretStr("set GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET")
    jwt_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    login: str
    name: str | None = None


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, User] = {}


db = Database()


def find_or_create_user(tokens: dict[str, Any], profile: dict[str, Any] | None) -> User | None:
    """GitHub says who logged in: our user for that account, created the first time."""
    del tokens  # GitHub's access token: keep it to call GitHub on the user's behalf
    if profile is None:
        return None  # refuses the login
    user_id = f"github:{profile['id']}"
    if user_id not in db.users:
        db.users[user_id] = User(id=user_id, login=profile["login"], name=profile.get("name"))
    return db.users[user_id]


def load_user(user_id: str) -> User | None:
    return db.users.get(user_id)


blocklist = TokenBlocklist()  # in FastAPICache's backend
auth = FastAPIAuth()
github = auth.use(
    OAuth2Strategy(
        name="github",
        authorization_url="https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize",
        token_url="https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token",  # noqa: S106  # a URL
        userinfo_url="https://api.github.com/user",
        client_id=settings.github_client_id,
        client_secret=settings.github_client_secret,
        redirect_uri=f"{settings.base_url}/auth/github/callback",
        scopes=["read:user"],
        verify=find_or_create_user,
    )
)
sessions = auth.use(SessionStrategy(load_user))
api_tokens = auth.use(
    JWTStrategy(
        settings.jwt_secret,
        issuer=settings.base_url,
        blocklist=blocklist,  # revoked tokens are refused
        verify=lambda claims: load_user(claims["sub"]),
    )
)

# Who makes the request, by each way the routes accept.
GitHubUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("github"))]
SessionUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session"))]
TokenUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("jwt"))]
AnyUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session", "jwt"))]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares sessions and revocations.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="auth", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware)  # session cookies: refuse what other sites make browsers send


@app.get("/login/github")
async def login() -> RedirectResponse:
    """To GitHub's login page, which sends the user back to the callback."""
    return github.redirect()


@app.get("/auth/github/callback")
async def github_callback(request: Request, user: GitHubUser) -> RedirectResponse:
    """GitHub sends the user back here: the strategy checks the state, exchanges the code and
    reads the profile; the session remembers the user from now on."""
    sessions.login(request, user.id)
    return RedirectResponse("/me", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def logout(request: Request, user: SessionUser) -> None:
    del user  # only to refuse requests without a session
    sessions.logout(request)


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: AnyUser) -> User:
    """With the session (a browser) or a token (a script)."""
    return user


class Token(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str = "bearer"  # noqa: S105  # the type of token, not one
    expires_in: int = TOKEN_LIFETIME


@app.post("/tokens", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def create_token(user: SessionUser) -> Token:
    """A token for the user's scripts. Only with the session: a token can't make tokens."""
    return Token(access_token=api_tokens.issue(user.id, expires_in=TOKEN_LIFETIME))


@app.delete("/tokens/current", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def revoke_token(
    user: TokenUser,
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())],
) -> None:
    """Refuse the request's token from now on, until it would have expired anyway."""
    del user  # checked by the JWT strategy: valid and not revoked
    claims = await api_tokens.decode(credentials.credentials)
    await blocklist.revoke(claims["jti"], expires_at=claims["exp"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: HTTPBearerStrategy
docs.text:
HTTPBearerStrategy Script to Your app: GET /me, Bearer pat_… Your app to Database: SHA-256(token) → user? Database to Your app: user 1. Your app to Script: 200 {"login": "octocat"}. Script to Your app: DELETE /tokens/current. Your app to Database: delete the digest. Script to Your app: GET /me, Bearer pat_… Your app to Script: 401: refused at once. The token says nothing by itself: delete its row, and it's dead. Script Your app Database GET /me, Bearer pat_… SHA-256(token) → user? user 1 200 {"login": "octocat"} DELETE /tokens/current delete the digest GET /me, Bearer pat_… 401: refused at once The token says nothing by itself: delete its row, and it's dead What it's for: tokens your app creates and looks up, such as personal access tokens, which stop working the moment they're deleted.

Personal access tokens: random strings that users create for their scripts, kept as digests, and refused as soon as they're deleted. The strategy: HTTPBearerStrategy.

From a clone of the repository:

source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Create a token as octocat, whose password is correct horse battery staple. It's shown this once: the database only keeps its digest.

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/tokens -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"login": "octocat", "password": "correct horse battery staple"}'
{"token":"pat_UrPE4G3pn56_cquuCHw2c52IcAn6X-4aYzCFvmvWohA","created_at":"2026-10-29T15:16:05.570276Z"}

A script sends it with each request:

$ TOKEN=pat_UrPE4G3pn56_cquuCHw2c52IcAn6X-4aYzCFvmvWohA
$ curl http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"id":"1","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

Delete it, and the next request with it is refused:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/tokens/current -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Digests, not tokens: the database keeps the SHA-256 of each token. Whoever reads it (a backup, a leak) gets nothing that works. The tokens are random and long, so a plain hash is enough: there's no password to guess.
  • Deleted, refused: unlike a JWT, the token carries nothing, so the app looks it up on each request. That costs a query, and buys taking a token back at once, in every process.
  • Before find_token: a token that isn't RFC 6750's syntax, or longer than 4 KiB, is refused without reaching your function.
  • A prefix: pat_ lets secret scanners (GitHub's, GitLab's) spot tokens leaked in code.
