docs.text:
PaginationTimeBased Client to Your app: GET /posts?timestamp=10:00Z. Your app to Database: < 10:00 DESC, LIMIT 4. Database to Your app: 09:30, then 3 at 09:00. Your app: 09:00 goes on: left for later. Your app to Client: 200, 1 post, next: 09:30. Client to Your app: GET ?timestamp=09:30Z. Your app to Client: 200, the three of 09:00. No item skipped, however many share a time. Client Your app Database GET /posts?timestamp=10:00Z < 10:00 DESC, LIMIT 4 09:30, then 3 at 09:00 09:00 goes on: left for later 200, 1 post, next: 09:30 GET ?timestamp=09:30Z 200, the three of 09:00 No item skipped, however many share a time What it's for: feeds and syncing by time, with pages that never split the items that share a time.

A cooperative's news feed by time: /posts newest first for readers, /posts/since oldest first for a client that syncs. A page never splits the posts that share a time, so the next one, which starts past it, skips none. The strategy: PaginationTimeBased.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.pagination.time_based:app

Nothing to configure: the timestamps aren't signed.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
The three newest posts, and in next_timestamp the time of the last one:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/posts"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
link: </posts?limit=3>; rel="first", </posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T10%3A00%3A00Z&limit=3>; rel="next"
etag: W/"fae4dd2eed51634151ef4bf0ef13c78a"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60

{"items":[{"title":"The bottling line is back","id":9,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T10:20:00Z"},{"title":"Recipe: salmorejo","id":8,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T10:00:00Z"},{"title":"Tasting at the cooperative","id":7,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T10:00:00Z"}],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":"2026-10-29T10:00:00Z"}

The posts before 10:00. The database returned four (the limit and one more), but the last two and the extra one share 09:00: they go together on the next page, and this one holds one post:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T10%3A00%3A00Z&limit=3"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
link: </posts?limit=3>; rel="first", </posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T09%3A30%3A00Z&limit=3>; rel="next"
etag: W/"966c6d24b7da1aec29fe05acdf5cfc6f"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60

{"items":[{"title":"The mill opens on Saturday","id":6,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T09:30:00Z"}],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":"2026-10-29T09:30:00Z"}

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T09%3A30%3A00Z&limit=3"
{"items":[{"title":"Price list: Arbequina","id":5,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T09:00:00Z"},{"title":"Price list: Hojiblanca","id":4,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T09:00:00Z"},{"title":"Price list: Picual","id":3,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T09:00:00Z"}],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":"2026-10-29T09:00:00Z"}

With pages of two, the three price lists can't fit in one, and splitting them would skip some: paginate raises ValueError, which the example answers with a 400:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T09:30:00Z&limit=2"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"More than 2 posts share a time: ask for more"}

A timestamp needs its time zone; any zone will do, and the same instant is the same cache entry:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T09:30:00"
{"detail":[{"type":"timezone_aware","loc":["query","timestamp"],"msg":"Input should have timezone info","input":"2026-10-29T09:30:00"}]}

$ curl -si "http://localhost:8000/posts?timestamp=2026-10-29T11:00:00%2B01:00" | grep cache-status
cache-status: Alcazaba; hit; ttl=56

Syncing, oldest first: the posts since 08:15. The first page stops before the three of 09:00:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/posts/since?timestamp=2026-10-29T08:15:00Z"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
link: </posts/since?limit=3>; rel="first", </posts/since?timestamp=2026-10-29T08%3A40%3A00Z&limit=3>; rel="next"
etag: W/"81b04e0669a930cbf1b7e03f6dbe168f"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60

{"items":[{"title":"Frost warning for the groves","id":2,"posted_at":"2026-10-29T08:40:00Z"}],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":"2026-10-29T08:40:00Z"}

At the end next_timestamp is null: the client keeps the time of the last post it got, and asks again later. A new post drops the cached pages (tag posts), and the next sync gets it:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/posts/since?timestamp=2026-10-29T10:20:00Z"
{"items":[],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":null}

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/posts -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Open day at the mill"}'
{"title":"Open day at the mill","id":10,"posted_at":"2026-10-30T09:21:45.133838Z"}

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/posts/since?timestamp=2026-10-29T10:20:00Z"
{"items":[{"title":"Open day at the mill","id":10,"posted_at":"2026-10-30T09:21:45.133838Z"}],"limit":3,"next_timestamp":null}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Two directions, two instances: PaginationTimeBased("older") for the feed (WHERE posted_at < :timestamp ORDER BY posted_at DESC) and PaginationTimeBased("newer") for syncing (WHERE posted_at > :timestamp ORDER BY posted_at).
  • Ties: the next page starts strictly past the last time, so a page never ends halfway through the posts of one time. With queried rows, the extra row shows when they go on, and the page leaves them all to the next one.
  • More than a page of one time: paginate raises ValueError rather than skip posts. If that can happen with your data, paginate by a unique key with PaginationKeyset (the time and the id).
  • Plain timestamps: ISO 8601 with a time zone, readable and writable by clients; the page's links put them in UTC, as the JSON does.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/time_based.py
"""A cooperative's news feed, by time: newest first for readers, oldest first for syncing.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.time_based:app

- `/posts`: the feed, newest first. `next_timestamp` is the time of the page's last post, and
  `?timestamp=<next_timestamp>` gives the posts before it.
- `/posts/since?timestamp=...`: the posts after a time, oldest first, for a client that syncs:
  it keeps the time of the last post it got, and asks for the ones after it.

Posts can share a time (the three price lists of 09:00 came in one import), and a page never
splits them: when they don't all fit, the page ends before them and the next one starts with
them all.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.time_based import (
    PaginationTimeBased,
    TimeBasedPage,
    TimeBasedParams,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class NewPost(BaseModel):
    title: str


class Post(NewPost):
    id: int
    posted_at: datetime


def posted_at(post: Post) -> datetime:
    return post.posted_at


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        news = [
            ("08:15", "The harvest starts in Jaén"),
            ("08:40", "Frost warning for the groves"),
            ("09:00", "Price list: Picual"),
            ("09:00", "Price list: Hojiblanca"),
            ("09:00", "Price list: Arbequina"),
            ("09:30", "The mill opens on Saturday"),
            ("10:00", "Tasting at the cooperative"),
            ("10:00", "Recipe: salmorejo"),
            ("10:20", "The bottling line is back"),
        ]
        self.posts = [
            Post(id=i, title=title, posted_at=datetime.fromisoformat(f"2026-10-29T{time}Z"))
            for i, (time, title) in enumerate(news, start=1)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def older(self, params: TimeBasedParams) -> list[Post]:
        """What a database does, through an index on posted_at:
        WHERE posted_at < :timestamp ORDER BY posted_at DESC LIMIT :fetch."""
        self.queries += 1
        timestamp = params.timestamp
        found = [p for p in self.posts if timestamp is None or p.posted_at < timestamp]
        return sorted(found, key=lambda p: (p.posted_at, p.id), reverse=True)[: params.fetch]

    def newer(self, params: TimeBasedParams) -> list[Post]:
        """WHERE posted_at > :timestamp ORDER BY posted_at LIMIT :fetch."""
        self.queries += 1
        timestamp = params.timestamp
        found = [p for p in self.posts if timestamp is None or p.posted_at > timestamp]
        return sorted(found, key=lambda p: (p.posted_at, p.id))[: params.fetch]

    def add(self, post: NewPost) -> Post:
        saved = Post(id=len(self.posts) + 1, title=post.title, posted_at=datetime.now(UTC))
        self.posts.append(saved)
        return saved


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the entries.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="news", vary_headers=())  # public data
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]

feed = PaginationTimeBased("older", default_limit=3, max_limit=50)
sync = PaginationTimeBased("newer", default_limit=3, max_limit=50)


def page(
    pages: PaginationTimeBased,
    rows: list[Post],
    params: TimeBasedParams,
) -> TimeBasedPage[Post]:
    try:
        return pages.paginate(rows, params, time=posted_at, queried=True)
    except ValueError:
        # More posts share one time than the page holds: a bigger page takes them.
        raise HTTPException(
            400,
            f"More than {params.limit} posts share a time: ask for more",
        ) from None


@app.get("/posts")
@cache(expire=60, tags=["posts"], exclude_params=["db"])
async def posts(
    params: Annotated[TimeBasedParams, Depends(feed)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
) -> TimeBasedPage[Post]:
    """Newest first: the posts before `timestamp`."""
    return page(feed, db.older(params), params)


@app.get("/posts/since")
@cache(expire=60, tags=["posts"], exclude_params=["db"])
async def posts_since(
    params: Annotated[TimeBasedParams, Depends(sync)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
) -> TimeBasedPage[Post]:
    """Oldest first: the posts after `timestamp`."""
    return page(sync, db.newer(params), params)


@app.post("/posts", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_post(post: NewPost, db: DatabaseDep) -> Post:
    """The newest post: the first page of the feed and the last of every sync change."""
    saved = db.add(post)
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags("posts")
    return saved


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("time_based:app", reload=True)

docs.title: PaginationToken
docs.text:
PaginationToken Client to Your app: GET /books?genre=poetry. Your app to Database: LIMIT 5 OFFSET 0. Your app to Client: 4 books, next_page_token. Client to Your app: …&page_token=WzQs… Your app: ✓ signature, query, age. Your app to Client: the next 4 books. Client to Your app: genre=novel, the same token. Your app to Client: 400: other query parameters. The token leads to the next page of its own query, and nowhere else. Client Your app Database GET /books?genre=poetry LIMIT 5 OFFSET 0 4 books, next_page_token …&page_token=WzQs… ✓ signature, query, age the next 4 books genre=novel, the same token 400: other query parameters The token leads to the next page of its own query, and nowhere else What it's for: a page at a time, where clients only send back the token the last page gave them: signed, bound to the query, and short-lived.

A library's books, a page at a time: the first request asks for a page size, and each page hands out a next_page_token for the one after. The token is opaque and signed, bound to the query it was issued for, and lasts ten minutes. Each page is cached for a minute. The strategy: PaginationToken.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.pagination.page_token:app

Set PAGE_TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without it each start makes up a throwaway one, and the tokens stop working when the app restarts, or on another process.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
The first page of poetry, four books, with the token of the next page in the body and in the Link header:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
link: </books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=WzQsIlpqSEdfOThjTnE4UWpGOHluQzJfYXciLDE3OTMzNTE4MjVd.i67GWpoWCJRwK-pdeD32Vw>; rel="next"
etag: W/"166a5b996896154fe0b3897c8c0f1a95"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60

{"items":[{"id":3,"title":"Book 3","genre":"poetry"},{"id":6,"title":"Book 6","genre":"poetry"},{"id":9,"title":"Book 9","genre":"poetry"},{"id":12,"title":"Book 12","genre":"poetry"}],"next_page_token":"WzQsIlpqSEdfOThjTnE4UWpGOHluQzJfYXciLDE3OTMzNTE4MjVd.i67GWpoWCJRwK-pdeD32Vw"}

The token, with the same query, gives the next page, cached like the first one, and so on until next_page_token is null:

$ TOKEN=WzQsIlpqSEdfOThjTnE4UWpGOHluQzJfYXciLDE3OTMzNTE4MjVd.i67GWpoWCJRwK-pdeD32Vw
$ curl "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=$TOKEN"
{"items":[{"id":15,"title":"Book 15","genre":"poetry"},{"id":18,"title":"Book 18","genre":"poetry"},{"id":21,"title":"Book 21","genre":"poetry"},{"id":24,"title":"Book 24","genre":"poetry"}],"next_page_token":"WzgsIlpqSEdfOThjTnE4UWpGOHluQzJfYXciLDE3OTMzNTE4MzVd.ejl-rzlIi-Zn5ai3MPncJA"}

$ curl -si "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=$TOKEN" | grep cache-status
cache-status: Alcazaba; hit; ttl=60

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=WzgsIlpqSEdfOThjTnE4UWpGOHluQzJfYXciLDE3OTMzNTE4MzVd.ejl-rzlIi-Zn5ai3MPncJA"
{"items":[{"id":27,"title":"Book 27","genre":"poetry"},{"id":30,"title":"Book 30","genre":"poetry"}],"next_page_token":null}

The token belongs to genre=poetry: with another genre, it's refused before anything is queried. So is a token whose offset a client changed (here, from 4 to 40), since the signature no longer matches:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=novel&page_size=4&page_token=$TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"page_token was issued for other query parameters"}

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=WzQwLCJaakhHXzk4Y05xOFFqRjh5bkMyX2F3IiwxNzkzMzUxODI1XQ.i67GWpoWCJRwK-pdeD32Vw"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"Invalid page_token"}

Ten minutes later, the first token has expired:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/books?genre=poetry&page_size=4&page_token=$TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"Expired page_token"}

Pages have a maximum size, checked before anything is queried:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/books?page_size=1000"
{"detail":[{"type":"less_than_equal","loc":["query","page_size"],"msg":"Input should be less than or equal to 50","input":"1000","ctx":{"le":50}}]}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Opaque, not secret: the token is base64 JSON and a signature. Its first part reads [4,"ZjHG_98cNq8QjF8ynC2_aw",1793351825]: the offset of the next page, the digest of the other query parameters (genre=poetry), and when it was issued. Clients are meant to send it back as it is; the signature (HMAC-SHA256) stops them from changing it.
  • Bound to the query: every query parameter but page_token and page_size counts, in any order, so a token never jumps to the middle of another list. page_size may change from one page to the next.
  • Short-lived: after ttl (600 seconds here) a token is a 400, and the client starts again from the first page. Nobody bookmarks page 40 of a list that has changed since.
  • From the database: params.offset and params.fetch (page_size plus one, which tells whether there's a next page) go into LIMIT :fetch OFFSET :offset, and paginate(rows, params, queried=True) makes the page and the next token.
  • Cached apart: the digest of the query is part of TokenParams, and so of the cache key: a page cached for one query never hands its token to another. A hit hands out the token issued when the page was cached, so keep the cache's expire well under the token's ttl.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/page_token.py
"""A library's books, paginated by page token: opaque, signed, bound to the query and short-lived.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.page_token:app

`/books?genre=poetry&page_size=3` answers the first page and its `next_page_token`; the next page
is `/books?genre=poetry&page_size=3&page_token=<next_page_token>`. A client can't make a token
up, use it with other filters (`genre=novel`), or keep it for more than ten minutes: any of these
is a 400. Each page is cached for a minute, under a key of its own.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.page_token import PaginationToken, TokenPage, TokenParams
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class Genre(StrEnum):
    # An enum, not any string: clients can't create cache entries without end.
    POETRY = "poetry"
    NOVEL = "novel"
    ESSAY = "essay"


class Book(BaseModel):
    id: int
    title: str
    genre: Genre


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        genres = list(Genre)
        self.books = [
            Book(id=i, title=f"Book {i}", genre=genres[i % len(genres)]) for i in range(1, 31)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def page(
        self,
        params: TokenParams,
        genre: Genre | None,
    ) -> list[Book]:
        """What a database does: WHERE genre = :genre ORDER BY id LIMIT :fetch OFFSET :offset."""
        self.queries += 1
        found = [book for book in self.books if genre is None or book.genre == genre]
        return found[params.offset : params.offset + params.fetch]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the entries.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="library", vary_headers=())  # public data
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    page_token_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()
# Signed: every process must have the same secret, or a token made by one is refused by the
# others: set PAGE_TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)). Ten minutes to read a list.
tokens = PaginationToken(
    settings.page_token_secret,
    ttl=600,
    default_page_size=10,
    max_page_size=50,
)


@app.get("/books")
@cache(expire=60, exclude_params=["db"])
async def books(
    params: Annotated[TokenParams, Depends(tokens)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
    genre: Genre | None = None,
) -> TokenPage[Book]:
    """By page token: each next_page_token gives the books after the page, for the same genre.
    The cache keeps every page of every query apart, and is kept for far less than the ten
    minutes a token lasts."""
    return tokens.paginate(db.page(params, genre), params, queried=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("page_token:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Secure by default
docs.text:
What could serve one user's data to another, trust data from outside, or let a client get around a protection is off unless you turn it on, and the documentation says what it costs.

The response cache is safe by default:

  • Users never get each other's responses. Requests carrying Authorization or Cookie get their own cache entries and the response is sent as Cache-Control: private, also when the endpoint authenticates through a router dependency.
  • No Redis script injection. FastAPICache.clear(namespace=...) deletes with SCAN + UNLINK: a namespace from user input never reaches a Lua script, and the server isn't blocked by KEYS.
  • Signed or encrypted entries. With a signing_key, every entry carries an HMAC bound to its key: whoever can write to Redis can't plant data, move one user's entry under another user's key, or get a pickle executed. With an encryption_key they're also encrypted (AES-256-GCM): a dump or a backup of Redis doesn't reveal the cached responses.
  • Bounded memory. InMemoryBackend evicts the least recently used entries instead of growing forever with every new query string.
  • Clients can't bypass the cache with Cache-Control: no-cache unless you allow it.
  • Only successful responses are cached, never a 404 or a 500 replayed as a 200.
  • Cache stampede protection: concurrent misses for one key compute once, in each process and, with distributed_lock, across processes.
  • A broken backend doesn't take the app down: every backend call has a timeout, and a circuit breaker stops calling it while it fails.
  • Keys that never repeat are reported: an argument whose repr() changes on every call (a database session, a service) makes every request a miss; Alcazaba warns about it.

And more: early refresh of popular entries, Valkey through valkey-py or Valkey GLIDE, cache hits that return the annotated type (Pydantic models, not dicts), deterministic ETags, the Cache-Status header (Alcazaba; hit; ttl=42, Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored), the response model in OpenAPI, exclude_params and stale-while-revalidate.

The other tools follow the same rules. Nothing that opens a door is stored in clear: API keys, one-time codes and revoked tokens are kept as digests or HMACs. Sessions keep only a random id in the cookie. Uploads are checked from their bytes, not from what the client says they are.

docs.title: Shared by every process
docs.text: An app runs in several processes, on several machines. Whatever must hold for all of them lives in the backend, Redis, Valkey, memcached or DynamoDB, and every process sees it at once: the rate limits and the locks, the sessions and the revoked tokens, maintenance mode and the feature flags. Scheduled jobs run once per tick whatever the number of processes, and the task queue runs each task at least once, retried when it fails.

docs.title: Resilient
docs.text: Every call to the backend has a timeout and goes through a circuit breaker: a backend that hangs or fails doesn't take the app down with it. What each tool does then is chosen for it and documented: the cache and the rate limiter let requests through, the token blocklist refuses them. The security model has the details.

docs.title: The FastAPI way
docs.text: The tools are what FastAPI already uses: dependencies (Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(...)), Depends(authz)), decorators (@cache) and ASGI middlewares. What they need from the request shows in the OpenAPI schema, and the docs' Authorize button knows the API keys and tokens. Everything is typed: @cache keeps the signature and the return type of what it decorates, and your editor completes what you write.

docs.title: Based on standards
docs.text: Errors are problem details (RFC 9457), cache results are told in Cache-Status (RFC 9211), and rate limits in the IETF's RateLimit headers. Webhooks follow Standard Webhooks, pages link to each other with Link (RFC 8288), and the security headers are OWASP's. Authorization uses Casbin policies, and metrics and traces go through OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: Observable
docs.text: Alcazaba logs under fastapi_alcazaba.* and, with the otel extra, records metrics and traces through OpenTelemetry: cache hits and misses, backend calls, limited requests, refused authorizations, task runs. Never keys, tokens or identities. Every request can have an ID, in the logs, the responses and the errors. See metrics and traces.

docs.title: Tested hard
docs.text: Every change runs the tests on Python 3.11 to 3.14, against real Redis, Valkey, a Valkey cluster, memcached and DynamoDB Local, with at least 90 % coverage, and the examples run in uvicorn processes against a real Valkey. Fuzzing (ClusterFuzzLite) runs on whatever reads data from outside, mutation testing checks that the tests notice when the code changes, and a benchmark 50 % slower than main's fails the pull request.

docs.title: Signed releases
docs.text: Releases are built by GitHub Actions and signed with Sigstore, with an SBOM of what they contain: you can verify that what PyPI serves is what the repository built. The project's builds take no dependency released less than three days earlier.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Each tool has a page in the Tutorial - User Guide, an example app and its reference.

  • Response cache

    @cache for endpoints and functions: one entry for everybody or one per user, invalidation by tag, signed or encrypted entries.

  • Backends

    In memory, Redis, Valkey, GLIDE, memcached or DynamoDB, and a copy in each process in front of them.

  • Pagination

    Twelve strategies: page numbers, offsets, ranges, cursors, keysets, ids, timestamps, sort values, tokens, scrolls and streams, each page cached under its own key.

  • Rate and concurrency limits

    Requests per window and requests at a time, per client or shared, across processes.

  • Idempotency keys

    A retried POST gets the first response instead of running twice.

  • Authentication strategies

    Who makes a request, by strategies: JWTs, bearer tokens, sessions, OAuth2 logins with GitHub or Google, SAML single sign-on, or your own.

  • API keys, tokens and codes

    API keys with scopes and expiry, a blocklist of tokens and one-time codes, nothing stored in clear.

  • Authorization with Casbin

    Who may do what, decided by a Casbin policy (ACL, RBAC, ABAC) per route or for every request.

  • Sessions, CSRF and security headers

    Sessions you can revoke, requests from other sites refused, the OWASP headers and a body size limit.

  • Audit trail

    Who did what to which resource, and whether it worked: no secrets, signed and chained.

  • Checking uploads

    The real type from the bytes, the size, image dimensions and safe file names.

  • Webhooks and outbound calls

    Standard Webhooks signing and verification, and calls out with a deadline, a breaker and SSRF protection.

  • Errors and observability

    RFC 9457 problem details, request IDs, timeouts, health checks, metrics and traces.

  • Background work

    Scheduled jobs, a task queue, a leader and locks, shared by every process.

  • Operations

    Circuit breakers, maintenance mode and feature flags that every process sees at once.

  • Security model and resilience

    What gets cached and for whom, what the backend is trusted with, and what happens when it fails.

docs.title: Tutorial - User Guide
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to use Alcazaba, step by step. It starts on this page with a quick start: a small shop API built in three steps, each adding one tool to the same main.py (a response cache, a rate limit and authorization with Casbin), each run and checked. The next pages take each tool in turn: read them in order, or go straight to the one you need.

Before you start

You need Python 3.11 or later, and to know FastAPI's basics: path operations, dependencies and the lifespan. If they're new to you, FastAPI's own tutorial explains them first.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Make a folder for the project, with a virtual environment, and install FastAPI and Alcazaba:

pipuv 
$ python -m venv .venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install "fastapi[standard]" "fastapi-alcazaba[casbin]"

$ uv venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ uv pip install "fastapi[standard]" "fastapi-alcazaba[casbin]"

fastapi[standard] brings the fastapi command and uvicorn, to run the app. Alcazaba itself only needs FastAPI; the casbin extra is for the third step.

docs.title: Create it
docs.text:
Create a file main.py with:

main.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


PRODUCTS = {1: Product(name="Olive oil", price=9.5)}


@app.get("/products/{product_id}")
@cache(expire=60)
async def read_product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return PRODUCTS[product_id]

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Run the development server:

$ fastapi dev main.py

 ⚡️ Starting FastAPI in development mode

 🐍 Using import string: main:app

 🌐 Server started at http://127.0.0.1:8000
    Documentation at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs

  Logs:

INFO:     Will watch for changes in these directories: ['/home/user/shop']
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
INFO:     Started reloader process [213542] using WatchFiles
INFO:     Started server process [213546]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.

It reloads the app whenever you save main.py: leave it running through the next steps.

With uvicorn

fastapi dev runs uvicorn for you. You can also run it yourself:

$ uvicorn main:app --reload

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In another terminal, ask for the product twice:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
etag: W/"d5c916899a1291fccfef605e3d4ede40"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60
vary: Authorization, Cookie

{"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
etag: W/"d5c916899a1291fccfef605e3d4ede40"
cache-status: Alcazaba; hit; ttl=60
cache-control: max-age=60
vary: Authorization, Cookie

{"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}

The first request ran read_product and stored its response: fwd=miss; stored. The second one came from the cache, hit, with the seconds the entry has left. A product that isn't there gets its 404, which is never cached:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/2
{"detail":"No such product"}

docs.title: Interactive API docs
docs.text: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs. FastAPI's interactive docs show the endpoint as usual: @cache keeps its parameters and its response model. Try it out twice, and look at the cache-status header of each response.

docs.title: Recap, step by step
docs.text:
FastAPICache.init(), in the lifespan, says where the entries live:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
    yield

InMemoryBackend keeps them in the process, which is enough to try things out. In production, Redis or Valkey keeps them for every process at once.

@cache(expire=60) keeps each response for 60 seconds:

@app.get("/products/{product_id}")
@cache(expire=60)
async def read_product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return PRODUCTS[product_id]

Under the route's decorator

@cache goes between @app.get(...) and the function. FastAPI registers the function below its decorator: with @cache above @app.get, the route would serve the uncached function.

Technical details

Each user gets entries of their own: requests with an Authorization or Cookie header have their own keys, and their responses are sent as Cache-Control: private. That's what vary: Authorization, Cookie tells browsers and proxies. Cache-Status is the header of RFC 9211, and the ETag lets clients revalidate with If-None-Match and get a 304 Not Modified. The response cache page has the rest: shared entries, keys, signed entries.

docs.title: Step 2: limit the rate
docs.text:
Reading a product is cheap now, but nothing stops a single client from taking all the server's time. Give each client five requests a minute:

main.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache, FastAPIRateLimiter
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


PRODUCTS = {1: Product(name="Olive oil", price=9.5)}


@app.get(
    "/products/{product_id}",
    dependencies=[Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(times=5, minutes=1))],
)
@cache(expire=60)
async def read_product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return PRODUCTS[product_id]

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
fastapi dev has reloaded the app. Make six requests:

$ for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1; done; echo
200 200 200 200 200 429

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
ratelimit: "5/60s";r=0;t=15
ratelimit-policy: "5/60s";q=5;w=60
retry-after: 15
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

The sixth request and those after it get a 429 Too Many Requests, with Retry-After: the seconds to wait. Every response carries the RateLimit header, so that clients can slow down before they get there: r is what's left, t the seconds until there's more.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
FastAPIRateLimiter is a FastAPI dependency: put it in dependencies=[...] of a route, of a router, or of the whole app. Dependencies run before the endpoint, so cached responses count too.

Behind a proxy

The limiter counts per client address, the one the ASGI server reports. Behind a proxy or a load balancer, tell uvicorn to take it from the proxy's headers (--forwarded-allow-ips); Rate limiting tells how, and how to count per user or per API key instead.

docs.title: Step 3: authorize with Casbin
docs.text:
Anybody may read the products, but only the staff may change their prices. Who's staff isn't written in the code: it's in a Casbin policy. Create these two files next to main.py:

model.confpolicy.csv model.conf
[request_definition]
r = sub, obj, act

[policy_definition]
p = sub, obj, act

[role_definition]
g = _, _

[policy_effect]
e = some(where (p.eft == allow))

[matchers]
m = g(r.sub, p.sub) && keyMatch2(r.obj, p.obj) && r.act == p.act
policy.csv
p, staff, /products/:id, PUT
g, ana, staff

The model says what a request is, (user, object, action), and when the policy allows it: when one of the user's roles (g) has a rule (p) whose path pattern matches the request's (keyMatch2, which takes :id for any value) and whose action is the request's. The policy says that the staff may PUT any product, and that Ana is staff.

Then use it in main.py:

main.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated

import casbin
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache, FastAPICasbin, FastAPIRateLimiter
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


PRODUCTS = {1: Product(name="Olive oil", price=9.5)}
TOKENS = {"ana-token": "ana", "ben-token": "ben"}  # stands in for your authentication


def current_user(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())],
) -> str:
    if credentials.credentials not in TOKENS:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid token", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return TOKENS[credentials.credentials]


here = Path(__file__).parent
enforcer = casbin.Enforcer(str(here / "model.conf"), str(here / "policy.csv"))
authz = FastAPICasbin(enforcer, subject=current_user)


@app.get(
    "/products/{product_id}",
    dependencies=[Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(times=5, minutes=1))],
)
@cache(expire=60, tags=lambda product_id, **_: [f"product:{product_id}"])
async def read_product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return PRODUCTS[product_id]


@app.put("/products/{product_id}", dependencies=[Depends(authz)])
async def update_product(product_id: int, product: Product) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    PRODUCTS[product_id] = product
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags(f"product:{product_id}")
    return product

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
Read the product, which caches it:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
{"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}

Then change its price without a token, as Ben, and as Ana:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name": "Olive oil", "price": 8.0}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ben-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name": "Olive oil", "price": 8.0}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Forbidden"}

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name": "Olive oil", "price": 8.0}'
{"name":"Olive oil","price":8.0}

And the product has its new price at once, although its old one was cached:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
ratelimit: "5/60s";r=3;t=2
ratelimit-policy: "5/60s";q=5;w=60
etag: W/"615d43a0044f76d19c5f354c5be3a495"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=60
vary: Authorization, Cookie

{"name":"Olive oil","price":8.0}

In the interactive docs, the PUT endpoint now has a lock: click Authorize, give ana-token, and try it out.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
FastAPICasbin takes the enforcer, which reads the model and the policy, and subject: a dependency that says who makes the request. current_user stands in for your authentication here; with yours, it decodes a JWT or reads a session.

here = Path(__file__).parent
enforcer = casbin.Enforcer(str(here / "model.conf"), str(here / "policy.csv"))
authz = FastAPICasbin(enforcer, subject=current_user)

Depends(authz) asks the policy about the request: may ana PUT /products/1? A request without a token gets a 401 before the policy is asked; one that the policy refuses, a 403.

Tags drop cached entries when the data changes: tags= names the product's entry, and FastAPICache.invalidate_tags() drops it after the update.

Your own actions

The path and the method aren't the only things to ask about: authz.require("prices", "change") asks whether the user may change prices, whatever the route. Authorization with Casbin tells how, and how to open routes to visitors without an account.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
You have an app whose product pages are cached and refreshed when they change, whose clients can't flood it, and whose prices only the staff can change:

  • FastAPICache.init() in the lifespan, and @cache(...) under the route's decorator.
  • FastAPIRateLimiter(...) in a route's dependencies.
  • FastAPICasbin(enforcer, subject=...) in a route's dependencies, with a Casbin model and policy.

In production

So far everything lives in the process: each process has its own cache and counters. With Redis or Valkey every process shares them, and a signing key keeps whoever can write to the backend from planting entries: see the production setup.
